Dispersion updates and starting values

Source: R/dispersion_calibration.R
dispersion_calibration.Rd

l0glmFit() estimates ordinary GLM dispersion and negative-binomial shape within the fit. Available information criteria use the returned noise parameter and count each fitted coefficient and estimated noise parameter.

Details

For an ordinary GLM with variance function \(V\) and weights \(w\), the Pearson target for \(\phi\) is $$\frac{1}{N-k}\sum_{i:w_i>0}\frac{w_i(y_i-\mu_i)^2}{V(\mu_i)}.$$ Here \(N\) counts observations with positive weight and \(k\) counts the fitted coefficient coordinates, including compulsory terms. Negative binomial with variance \(\mu+\mu^2/\theta\) solves the corresponding weighted Pearson equation with target \(\bar w(N-k)\). Its left hand side increases with \(\theta\), so the solver uses a bounded scalar root. Fixed dispersion or shape values stay fixed.

During adaptive-ridge selection the updates begin at iteration three once \(k < 0.7N\). A step can change the noise parameter by a factor between one half and two. Three successive changes within one percent of the target pause the updates until the support changes. A relaxed pass uses the full Pearson target with positive residual degrees of freedom. These are residual moment estimates. The coefficient step and noise step need not maximize the joint likelihood.

The default control.family=list(dispersion.calibration="auto") enables the following starting values. Set the entry to FALSE to use the ordinary initializers. TRUE enables the same eligible pilots as "auto". The Pearson updates run with either choice.

  • Signed, grouped Gaussian identity-link fits with multiple channels and between \(n+1\) and \(10n\) selectable predictors use five adaptive-ridge steps with shared row norms. The last local ridge smoother supplies a residual scale for each channel. The subsequent fit uses the BIC preset if lambda was omitted. The pilot needs an in-memory unscreened fit, at least five allowed iterations and automatic starts and dispersions. It leaves explicit group specifications to the predictor-group interface.

  • A five-step Poisson fit with the same link supplies starting values for automatic negative-binomial log-link fits. For direct nonnegative identity-link fits it supplies only the starting shape. A fixed or non-default starting shape, supplied coefficients or prior means, or preclustering uses the ordinary initializer.

A constrained negative-binomial unpenalized refit checks conditional likelihood descent when coefficients touch the boundary. If the clipped working solution stalls, the refit tries a diagonally scaled projected score step within the same support.

See the information criteria for the role of model-space size. The wide Gaussian BIC preset is motivated by multitask examples where each selected row adds many fitted coefficients. Screened fits retain their usual GIC preset.
